question: How many new judges were sworn-in to the Supreme Court of India on 30 May 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**two**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **On 30 May 2025, two new judges were sworn-in to the Supreme Court of India.** This addition was aimed at maintaining efficiency in the apex court's functioning and addressing the backlog of cases.
 
• The Supreme Court of India is the highest judicial authority in the country, consisting of the Chief Justice of India and other judges appointed by the President of India as per Article 124 of the Constitution.
 
• Judges of the Supreme Court are appointed based on their qualifications, experience, and recommendations from the Collegium system.
 
• The swearing-in of new judges is an important event as it strengthens the judiciary and ensures timely justice delivery.
 
• The appointment of judges is crucial for maintaining the balance and independence of the judiciary, which is one of the pillars of democracy in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Supreme Court Composition:**

 
 
• The Supreme Court can have a maximum strength of 34 judges, including the Chief Justice of India, as per the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019.
 
• Judges are appointed by the President based on recommendations of the Collegium system, comprising senior judges of the Supreme Court.
 
 
 
• **Collegium System:**
 
 
• The Collegium system is responsible for the appointment and transfer of judges in the higher judiciary. It comprises the Chief Justice of India and four senior-most judges of the Supreme Court.
 
• This system ensures transparency and independence in the selection process.
 
 
 
• **Qualifications for Supreme Court Judges:**
 
 
• A judge must be a citizen of India and have served as a High Court judge for at least five years or been an advocate in a High Court for ten years.
 
• Alternatively, the person must be considered a distinguished jurist by the President of India.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Backlog:**
 
 
• The addition of judges to the Supreme Court is essential to address the backlog of pending cases. As of recent statistics, the court handles thousands of cases annually.
 
• The appointment of judges helps in streamlining case management and ensuring speedy justice.
 
 
 
• **Role of Supreme Court:**
 
 
• The Supreme Court is tasked with upholding the Constitution of India, resolving disputes between states, and protecting fundamental rights of citizens.
 
• It acts as the guardian of the Constitution and ensures the rule of law in the country.
